newsitem.title: IRAN: Mideast OPEC states need new oil policy - Varzi.
newsitem.headline: Mideast OPEC states need new oil policy - Varzi.

text.p: OPEC's Middle East giants are in danger of allowing their massive oil reserves to lay fallow for sometime to come if they do not quickly adopt policies to attract fresh investments, a leading oil analyst said on Friday.

"There is a real danger the Middle East will not fulfill its potential unless the right fiscal and legislative policies are in place," said London-based Mehdi Varzi, chief oil analyst at finance house Kleinwort Benson.
"Do not rely on the market to bail you out. The way to compete with non-OPEC is to attract investments," he told an energy conference in Isfahan.

OPEC's large Middle East producers -- Saudi Arabia, Iran, the United Arab Emirates and Kuwait -- in recent years have seen non-OPEC producers, and some OPEC colleagues, take a rising share of world output at their expense.
By contrast, OPEC nations like Venezuela have attracted a rush of foreign oil companies, boosting output and taking extra markets share.
"Some OPEC members now are behaving like non-OPEC producers," said Varzi.
He said OPEC's role in trying to balance world markets has become outdated by an oil futures market also concerned with offsetting risks in other financial sectors.
"OPEC is addressing the new issues with the old policies," Varzi said.
"Vital Western markets, far from becoming more reliant on the Middle East, were becoming less dependent on the region".
"The Atlantic basin is developing a dynamic of its own, becoming more self-sufficient," he said.
Varzi said Mideast producers must unlock their own domestic investment potential in tandem with foreign company investment.
"As long as government retains monopoly control of the oil and gas sectors it will not provide proper returns," he said.
He said international upstream investments now were focused mainly in higher cost, no-OPEC regions because incentives there were greater.
"Those who produce more are those who offer the incentives," he said.
